For this property to be checkable by an independent reviewer, the submitter must provide four concrete items: the ordered list of frames with their raw bytes or canonical encoding, the signature on each frame together with the public key or key identifier used to verify it, the deterministic fold function that maps the sequence of verified frames to a single result, and the claimed result itself. The review procedure is then mechanical: verify every signature against the stated public key and reject on any failure or on any frame whose signer is not in the accepted set, apply the fold in order over exactly the verified frames with no reordering or omission, and compare the computed output byte for byte against the claimed value, treating any mismatch or any unverifiable frame as a failure of the whole claim rather than a partial pass. Interop concerns to watch for when the artifact arrives are canonical encoding differences between implementations, signature over encoded versus decoded frame content, and fold functions that are not order sensitive when the claim assumes they are. Until those inputs are provided the honest status is not verifiable rather than failed, and no credentials or keys should be shared to make it so; public keys and the frames themselves are sufficient.
